hint: Base the evaluation on data analytics; focus on how data can determine whether a feature is being adopted as intended and delivering measurable user or business value.

question: Design an app for sports enthusiasts.
hint: One approach: focus on booking sports facilities. Address both demand and supply sides, map user needs and pain points, propose features with a priority matrix and success metrics, and split the solution into an MVP and full-release roadmap.

question: Design a smart dustbin and create a go-to-market plan to launch it.
hint: Set the target market first, identify pressing and aspirational needs around waste disposal, design the MVP, define success metrics, then build a GTM strategy covering marketing channels and service model.

question: Design an app for pet parents.
hint: Start with clarifying questions (geography, OS, type of pet), apply CIRCLES, choose a target persona, justify your assumptions, and map pain points to prioritised feature solutions.

question: An OTT streaming service is losing subscribers. What are the possible reasons?
hint: Start with clarifying questions, then explore both internal factors (content library, pricing, UX) and external factors (competition, macro trends). The interviewer wanted breadth of factors with sound reasoning rather than a single definitive root cause.

question: How should Winzo enter the US market?
hint: Cover target market selection, legal entity structure, tax and regulatory implications (especially gambling laws), profit repatriation, competitive risks from US gaming incumbents, and launch promotions.

question: What metrics would you use to measure the success of a newly launched app after six months?
hint: Key metrics: daily active users, number of users acquired, and retention rate. Tailor the choice to the app's core loop and business model.

question: Walk me through your critique of the Winzo app — what do you like and what would you improve?
hint: Highlight differentiating features (variety of games, regional language content, user nudges) and suggest improvements like building in-app communities and expanding multiplayer game modes.

question: The revenue of your favourite gaming app is declining. Identify the reasons and list the metrics you would track.
hint: Pick a specific game (e.g., Candy Crush) and run a structured RCA. Understand the core game loop first. Use gaming-specific metrics such as DAU, ARPDAU, session length, D1/D7/D30 retention, and monetisation funnel conversion.

question: Downloads of Spotify are decreasing in Europe. How would you identify the reasons?
hint: Divide the problem into content creators and content consumers and explore factors on each side. The interviewer valued breadth of thinking over a single root cause.

question: Estimate the total number of Google searches made in India in a single day.
hint: Segment users by age group, estimate hours spent online per group, assume a search frequency (e.g., one search per 15 minutes online), then aggregate. Apply rural/urban split and internet penetration rates to size each population segment.

question: Swiggy's revenue has dropped by 10%. Identify the root cause using the fewest possible diagnostic steps.
hint: Decompose revenue into DAU × ARPDAU, then further break down DAU (new installs + returning users) and ARPDAU (ARPPU × conversion rate). Pick one lever at a time and drill down through the customer journey funnel.

question: Give five reasons why Snakes and Ladders is still an engaging game, and then propose improvements to make it more attractive to modern players.
hint: Part A: identify what the game delivers — uncertainty, thrill, ease of learning, short session length, and head-to-head competition — and explain how each drives engagement through game psychology. Part B: pick one dimension (e.g., thrill) and design a feature that amplifies it.

question: As the PM for a clothing retail store, what data points would you want to collect, and how would you organise them for business use?
hint: Scope the business context first (geography, channels, merchandise type). Identify data dimensions: customer, geography, product, time, and sales. Map each to a source such as EPOS, online sales, supplier purchases, and customer social profiles.

question: Estimate the number of flights departing from Delhi's Indira Gandhi International Airport in a single day.
What is your favourite product, how would you improve it, and what metrics would you use to measure success?
hint: Pick a product you genuinely use and know well. Identify a specific problem you personally face, propose one targeted improvement, and tie success metrics directly to the improvement's intended outcome.

question: Pick one SaaS product and propose a single improvement. Include the problem to be solved, how to validate the hypothesis, the data you would look at, success metrics, and mocks.
hint: Align your choice with the company's values (collaboration tools). Clarity on the 'what and why' of the problem is more important than the solution. Wireframe mocks show effort and are strongly recommended.

question: Spotify wants to create a new income stream without relying on advertising or premium subscriptions. What would you suggest?
hint: Clarify the objective is a net-new revenue stream. Segment users into casual and hardcore fans, prioritise hardcore for higher willingness to pay. Evaluate options (ticketed live events, music teaching, exclusive superfan spaces) and align the final choice with Spotify's strategic goals.

question: How would you price the new Spotify income stream features you just proposed?
hint: Walk through cost-plus (marginal cost ≈ 0, so less applicable), competitor-based (benchmark against Patreon), and value-based pricing. Justify your recommendation with reference to user willingness to pay and business alignment.

question: How do you prioritise between competing product features when resources are limited? Walk me through your framework and give a real example.
hint: Check business goal alignment first, then apply RICE scoring. Highlight exigencies — legal requirements or resource constraints — that might override the framework. Ground the answer in a concrete career example.

question: How would you monetise Fantasy Premier League?
hint: Research play-to-earn and fantasy sports monetisation models. Present ideas with clear logical reasoning (e.g., premium leagues, in-game item purchases, sponsored challenges), and be ready to defend each idea under cross-examination.

question: How would you increase engagement among Dream11 or Fantasy Premier League users during international football breaks when no live matches are being played?
hint: Focus on social and community features — head-to-head prediction contests, squad discussion forums, or historical data challenges — that sustain platform habit even without live games.

question: Design an influencer programme for Dream11.
hint: Apply CIRCLES. Map the influencer journey from onboarding to content creation to reward, and explain how the programme supports Dream11's acquisition and retention goals.

question: A SaaS start-up wants to enter the Communication and Engagement industry. How can it succeed?
hint: Assess the competitive landscape (fragmented market, no dominant player, low customer satisfaction). Identify core pain points and design an offering that addresses them in a differentiated way.

question: What factors would you consider when deciding what to build next, given severely constrained engineering resources?
As a PM at Swiggy, how would you solve the problem of allowing customers to order from multiple restaurants in a single transaction?
hint: Identify the affected user segments and use cases. List candidate solutions and flag implementation pitfalls such as differing delivery times, split payments, and restaurant coordination complexity.

question: How would you measure the success of a multi-restaurant ordering feature on Swiggy?
hint: Divide metrics into north star, L1, and L2 layers. Explain why each level of granularity matters for product decision-making.

question: How would you plan the release of a multi-restaurant ordering feature on Swiggy?
hint: Outline both pre-launch and launch activities, covering supply-side (restaurant onboarding, logistics) and demand-side (user communication, promotions) initiatives. Define success metrics for each activity.

question: Cart abandonment on Myntra has increased significantly over the past month. How would you find out why?
hint: First clarify what counts as cart abandonment. Rule out external factors, then map the checkout funnel step by step, identifying where drop-offs are occurring and listing potential causes for each stage.

question: You ship two features simultaneously, both designed to improve the same metric. How do you determine which one is more effective?
hint: Use A/B testing — assign distinct user cohorts to each feature so their impact on the shared metric can be measured independently.

question: Your design team wants to ship an elaborate new design, but the engineering team strongly disagrees with the scope. How do you resolve this?
As a PM, would you always pursue a product-led growth strategy, or are there situations where you would not?
Redesign the homepage of the Netflix Android app.
hint: Apply a modified CIRCLES framework: clarify the goal first (e.g., improve content discovery or increase watch time), walk through the current user journey, then propose and prioritise design changes.

question: Design a bill payment feature for a neobank app.
hint: Clarify the strategic goal (e.g., increase app stickiness/daily utility). Ask scoping questions, keep the session conversational, and explore out-of-the-box options beyond standard bill reminders.

question: You are a PM at The Ken, a digital media publication. What metrics would you include in a 'happiness index' for its readers?
hint: Segment the product by channel (mobile app, desktop, newsletter). List L1 metrics for each channel, then drill to specific low-level metrics. Use AARRR to ensure completeness and justify the relevance of each metric.

question: Readership numbers across The Ken's products are declining. How would you diagnose the problem?
hint: Think out loud rather than following a rigid structure. Explore content-side factors (quality, topic relevance, publish cadence), platform-side factors (UX, notifications, discovery), and external competitive factors.

question: Estimate Facebook's total advertising revenue in India for one year.
hint: Top-down approach: total Facebook users in India → active users → daily sessions per user → ads per session → click-through rate → cost per click. Discuss assumed values with the interviewer and calculate to a final number.

question: Critique the Google Pay app and propose improvements.
hint: Open the app live and do a walking critique. Before suggesting changes, clarify the objective and target user. Focus on habit-forming UX (e.g., group payments, bill reminders, decluttered home screen) and benchmark against Paytm and PhonePe.

question: You are a PM at Google Pay. Propose a strategy to ensure Google Pay remains a market leader and redesign the app's homepage to support that strategy.
hint: Ground your strategy in a clear market positioning thesis. Justify every homepage design decision with a specific user need or strategic goal; the interviewer will probe each wireframe element.

question: A feature you shipped had strong adoption for three months but engagement has dropped sharply over the past two weeks. What are the possible causes?
hint: Clarify what 'engagement' means precisely. Eliminate external factors first, then explore product-level issues (bugs, UX regressions, notification changes) and app-level changes. Use the interviewer's responses to narrow down hypotheses and list confirming metrics.

question: What are the top three metrics you would track for Instagram Live, and why?
hint: State why Instagram Live was introduced. Identify two user types — creators and viewers — and list three key metrics per side, balancing reach, engagement, and interaction quality.

question: How would you increase the number of paid Spotify subscribers in India?
hint: Clarify the current offering. Segment users and identify barriers to conversion. Propose growth strategies such as telco bundling, tiered pricing, student/family plans, and partnerships rather than purely feature-driven solutions.

question: You are a PM at Facebook. How would you improve the Facebook app's experience to better serve users who are seeking romantic connections?
hint: Ask 5-7 clarifying questions to narrow the scope (platform, objective: increase retention). Focus on the 18-30 age group. Leverage Facebook's real-world social graph to make online matching safer. Follow with success metrics and risk assessment.

question: Estimate the number of tube lights in Delhi.
hint: Take constant feedback and ask clarifying questions upfront. Explain your approach step by step — the method and structure matter more than the final number.

question: How would you design the restaurant search and discovery experience on Google for users during the COVID-19 pandemic?
hint: Define Google's mission and goal first. Identify COVID-specific user pain points (safety info, delivery availability, capacity limits). Apply CIRCLES to generate solutions and use Impact/Effort prioritisation.

question: Define the key success metrics for the Gmail mobile app.
hint: Apply the AARRR framework to structure metrics across the full user lifecycle — acquisition, activation (first email sent/read), retention, revenue (Workspace upsell), and referral.

question: Daily Active Users on the Gmail mobile app have dropped by 5%. How would you diagnose the cause?
hint: Investigate external factors (iOS/Android platform changes, competition, seasonality) and internal factors (app bugs, notification policy changes, UX regressions). Propose metrics that would confirm or rule out each hypothesis.

question: Estimate the total number of flights taking off from all airports across India in one hour.
hint: Approach: number of airports × average number of runways per airport × operational hours % × capacity utilisation × average takeoff turnaround time.

question: How would you redesign the college dormitory laundry experience?
Should Google enter the e-learning business? Walk me through your analysis.
hint: Structure: clarify the question, restate Google's mission, define goals, assess strengths and weaknesses, apply Porter's Five Forces, identify risks and mitigations, then deliver a clear strategic recommendation.

question: You have invented magical boots that allow an average person to run as fast as Usain Bolt. What would you do next?
hint: Ask clarifying questions, define goals (revenue, mass adoption). Apply Porter's Five Forces to assess the market landscape, then define target segments, positioning, pricing, and distribution channels.

question: You are the PM for a mobile Ludo game. There has been a sudden dip in the number of active users. Find out why.
hint: Clarify what 'users' means and how 'dip' is defined. Explore internal factors (product changes, monetisation friction, bugs) and then external factors (seasonality, competition). Keep the discussion conversational.

question: What metrics would you track if you were the PM of a mobile Ludo game?
hint: Use AARRR: acquisition (installs), activation (first completed game), retention (D1/D7/D30 return sessions), revenue (in-app chip purchases), and referral (invite mechanics).

question: As PM of a mobile Ludo game, you notice a sudden drop in in-game currency (chip) purchases. Find out why.
hint: Precisely define the drop. Explore internal factors (chip pricing changes, placement, purchase flow friction) and external factors (competitor promotions, platform billing changes).

question: How would you redesign the in-game currency purchase experience in a mobile Ludo game to increase conversions?
hint: Map where chips are currently presented in the game. Identify high-intent moments in the user journey where players want chips but are not prompted. Propose contextual placements and incentives aligned with those moments.

question: Design a mobile game targeted at women aged 45–60.
hint: Apply CIRCLES. Deep-dive into the persona's motivations, preferences, and pain points before proposing features — empathy with this specific demographic is what the interviewer is evaluating.

question: You are the PM at LinkedIn. Daily Active Users have dropped. Identify the root cause and propose solutions.
Flipkart is launching an e-commerce app for first-time online shoppers in Tier 2 and Tier 3 Indian cities. Walk me through the key components you would design for the app.
hint: Clarify assumptions (vernacular language, e.g., Hindi). Focus on home page structure: Search, Major Categories, Deals, and Add-to-Cart. Use pictorial/icon-based design for low-digital-literacy users. Address address-entry for users unfamiliar with form inputs.

question: Discuss your favourite product and suggest one improvement that would drive meaningful user growth.
hint: Pick a product you know deeply (e.g., Spotify). Identify a specific unmet use case using CIRCLES logic (e.g., collaborative listening), design a feature addressing it, and explain the growth mechanism.

question: Design an enterprise search engine for a large organisation.
hint: Apply CIRCLES but expect deep technical follow-ups: how to parse different file types, integrate with enterprise systems (Outlook, SharePoint, Slack), and handle technical constraints like access permissions and indexing latency.

question: Microsoft has access to rich data about users' preferences, contacts, and daily schedules. Using this data and AI, design a new product.
hint: Work backwards from the technology: identify use cases where this data is most valuable. Define a clear objective (e.g., increasing corporate productivity) and design features grounded in that goal.

question: Design a travel platform for Microsoft, keeping in mind the constraints and behaviours introduced by the COVID-19 pandemic.
hint: Clarify the target user (enterprise vs. consumer). Consider how pandemic constraints (remote work, safety concerns, travel restrictions) change traveller needs. Identify existing Microsoft products (Teams, Bing, Azure) that could be leveraged.

question: You are the PM at Amazon. How would you tackle the problem of fake product reviews?
hint: Define what counts as a fake review and how to detect it. Map the motivations of bad actors (seller manipulation, competitor sabotage). Assess business impact. Propose prioritised solutions based on impact and ease of implementation.

question: Design an online platform for working professionals who want to learn to play a musical instrument.
hint: Follow a standard design approach but expect scope changes mid-interview. Draw wireframes when prompted. Consider both the learner journey and the instructor/content-provider experience.

question: Design a browsing experience for users who are completely offline.
hint: Carefully scope the user segment (intermittent vs. permanently offline). Identify which browsing behaviours must be preserved, what data can be cached pre-emptively, and how sync and conflict resolution work when connectivity returns.

question: Design a general-purpose monitoring service for web applications.
hint: Start from first principles: draw a typical web app architecture, list metrics to expose per component, then design alerting and dashboarding. For GTM, propose a SaaS model with freemium tiers and bottom-up developer marketing.

question: Microsoft wants to achieve 10x growth for MS Teams in the consumer market. As the PM for Teams, how would you approach this challenge?
hint: Invest significant time in user segmentation. Target internet-based interest and hobby groups to exploit network effects. Set new user signups as the north star metric, with engagement and retention parameters as L1 metrics.

question: You are a PM on the MS Office team and have access to a cross-product usage graph for all Microsoft products. How would you use this data to improve the Office user experience?
hint: Clarify scope and target user. Segment users behaviourally. Use cross-product usage patterns to identify workflow gaps and feature adoption drop-offs, then propose targeted improvements grounded in the data insights.

question: You have 100 product requirements but only engineering bandwidth to build 30. How do you decide what gets built?
How would you determine the optimal minimum order value below which a delivery charge should be applied on a fashion e-commerce platform?
hint: Focus on the logical framework for arriving at a threshold rather than the exact number. Consider average order values, per-order delivery cost, margin contribution, and the conversion impact of the threshold.

question: What metrics would you use to compare the effectiveness of two different free-shipping threshold values against each other?
You are the PM at Facebook. Design a feature specifically for elderly users (65+).
Estimate the area of the parking lot at a major international airport such as Delhi's Indira Gandhi International Airport.
hint: Approach 1: estimate plane count × average plane capacity × peak occupancy to derive parking demand, then convert to area. Approach 2: use gate count × flow rate. Demonstrating multiple estimation approaches is valued.

question: You are the CEO of an insurance company and have noticed a sudden surge in claims. How would you decide whether to continue or exit the business?
hint: Clarify the magnitude, type, and timing of the increase. Explore reasons for the surge (seasonal patterns, macro events, adverse selection). Frame the go/no-go decision around whether claim payouts exceed premium revenue and long-term actuarial viability.

question: Design a digital product for the blue-collar workforce and outline how you would bring it to market.
hint: Define a clear business goal and pick a focused vertical (e.g., vocational training for electricians and plumbers). Design MVP features (progress tracking, assessments, job placements) and outline a GTM strategy. Weigh B2C vs. B2B trade-offs.

question: Should Netflix enter the personal video uploads market, similar to YouTube?
Flipkart has seen a 30% drop in sales in its electronics category over the last month. As the product manager, how would you investigate and address this?
hint: Ask clarifying questions about UI changes and competitor promotions. Trace the customer journey funnel to find the stage where traffic dropped most sharply, then deep-dive into solutions specific to that stage rather than applying a generic framework.

question: What design changes would you make to increase the attachment rate of add-on services such as extended warranty on an e-commerce product page?
hint: Suggested levers include defaulting the add-on to opted-in, partnering with banks for bundled offers, and adding a short product-page video illustrating the financial risk of skipping the add-on.

question: Conversion rates are dropping on an e-commerce site. Walk me through how you would diagnose the root cause.
hint: Bucket issues into tech, business, and operational categories and build separate problem trees for each. Track metrics across all three dimensions—conversion drops can stem from vendor shortages or logistics failures, not just engineering bugs.

question: How would you improve your favourite product, and what metrics would you use to evaluate the success of any new feature you introduce? (Candidate used Spotify.)
How would you fit into an individual-contributor product role after leading teams for more than seven years?
How can OLX improve its product and service in India, and how specifically could you contribute to that?

You are the PM for the OYO app. You want to grow platform revenue through off-platform and on-screen push notifications. How would you approach this, and what content would you ideate for these pop-ups?
hint: Clarify whether the target is lapsed users or frequent customers, then build three user personas and prioritise one aligned to the north-star revenue metric. Map their journey, surface pain points at each step, and design pop-up content addressing those points. Define drop-out rate metrics at every journey stage.

question: Design a loyalty programme for Amazon Prime that spans its full ecosystem—Prime Video, shopping, Kindle, and beyond.
hint: Profile users across each ecosystem, identify a key unmet need per user type, and design cross-ecosystem bundling solutions built around exclusivity to deepen engagement and switching costs.

question: You are the PM for a large on-demand food delivery platform in India. The day after a major holiday—historically a peak period—you see a 35% drop in orders. What factors drive overall orders, what could explain the drop, and how would you stack-rank the possible causes? What metrics beyond total order count would you examine?
hint: Separate internal from external factors and use a customer-journey funnel to isolate the stage that broke. Supplement total-orders data with session counts, cart-abandonment rate, delivery-partner availability, restaurant uptime, and payment failure rates to triangulate the root cause.

question: You are the PM at Gmail. Define and present a one-year product roadmap with a primary goal of customer acquisition.
hint: Establish market size, growth target, and competitive landscape first. Structure the roadmap across four quarters: Q1 for tech-debt paydown and must-have feature discovery, Q2–Q3 for beta launch and validation, Q4 for full launch. Be ready to discuss resourcing and financial trade-offs.

question: As the PM of PhonePe's payment-gateway product, how would you increase transaction revenue from the merchant side—for example, merchants like Swiggy?
How would you improve Google Maps for both engagement and monetisation?
What would be the key success metrics for Swiggy as a business?
How would you improve Swiggy's engagement metrics?
hint: Explain the reasoning behind each metric choice and how metrics act as proxy signals—for example, rising delivery ETAs on Swiggy may signal delivery-partner churn to Zomato, indicating a competitive threat.

question: Design a loyalty programme for the PhonePe merchant platform.
hint: Apply the CIRCLES framework: identify merchant needs and the business case, brainstorm solutions, and prioritise. Be ready to follow up with a system-architecture discussion—how components communicate, query frequency, and processing load.

question: Design a cyber-security plan for a large healthcare provider, and explain how you would convey the ROI of such a project to executive leadership.
hint: Ask about HIPAA constraints and internal data-usage policies. Propose a cloud-based plan covering identity and access management, threat assessment and remediation of existing systems, and creation of mitigation and recovery plans. Frame ROI in terms of quantified risk reduction and regulatory compliance value.

question: How would you design a product or system that eliminates the need for patients to carry physical medical files between hospitals?
hint: Describe primary and secondary research methods, anticipate challenges such as multi-stakeholder buy-in, data standardisation, and capital requirements. Propose a government-partnership model and outline a pitch with a proof-of-concept approach.

question: As a Growth and Monetisation PM at a fitness start-up, how would you develop a plan to kick-start growth and monetise the product?
You are the PM at Finshots, a financial news start-up. Develop a monetisation plan for the product.
hint: Walk through the 5Cs of the industry context, then apply the 4Ps framework to propose a couple of monetisation plans. Drill into the areas the interviewer shows most interest in rather than covering everything shallowly.

question: How many active Swiggy delivery partners are there in Bangalore right now?
hint: Clarify scope (full-time vs part-time partners, exact city boundaries), split Bangalore into urban and suburban zones, estimate daily orders per zone, average deliveries per partner per day, and derive total headcount needed.

question: How would you launch Zomato in a tier-2 Indian city? What launch metrics would you define, and over what time horizons?
hint: Divide the launch into three parallel tracks: customers, delivery partners, and restaurants. Apply a new-product-launch structure to each. Define metrics at one-week, one-month, three-month, and six-month milestones per segment.

question: Design a product to improve the physical health of users.
hint: One strong answer was a remote-caring application synced with wearables—smartwatch or fitness band—that enables family members to monitor and receive health reports for elderly relatives from a distance.

question: Design a fitness-channel feature for Netflix.
hint: Leverage Netflix's existing recommendation engine to create a curated fitness channel, with a focus on children who shifted to sedentary gaming habits during COVID. Use existing video library assets to bring physical activities into the home.

question: Design a travel product for Facebook.
hint: Harness Facebook's user-data graph and existing Groups infrastructure to tackle trip planning and the travel experience—specifically to save time and eliminate contradictions that arise in collaborative group-trip planning.

question: Swiggy's platform traffic dropped sharply and significantly last week. Conduct a root-cause analysis.
hint: Rule out external or seasonal factors first because the drop is sudden. Then trace internal factors stage by stage through the customer-journey funnel—app open, search, cart, checkout, payment—to isolate where users are falling off.

question: How would you improve the Swiggy app? Once you've identified a new feature, how would you roll it out, measure its success, and identify the right early adopters?
hint: Explore the social dimensions of food ordering for improvement ideas. For roll-out, compare A/B testing, phased release, and other experimental methods along with their trade-offs. Define success metrics tied to the north-star, and profile early adopters based on alignment with platform goals.

question: Estimate the total market size for a European EV battery manufacturer entering the Indian electric four-wheeler market.
hint: Narrow scope to four-wheelers. Segment India's population by urban/rural and income class, estimate vehicle ownership per segment, exclude low-income households for EV relevance, and use a 10-year vehicle lifecycle to convert total stock into an annual replacement market.

question: As the Swiggy Instamart PM, how would you measure customer perception of Instamart's discounts relative to BigBasket, and what would you do to change that perception if needed?
hint: Use two levers: a conjoint-style customer survey comparing Instamart and BigBasket on value perception, plus focus groups; and marketing experiments A/B testing discount-themed push notifications against non-discount ones, measuring order volume and basket size lift.

question: You work at a kids' furniture shop. Design a bookshelf for children—define your target audience, describe the design, and specify the metrics you would track.
hint: Identify pain points for both parents and children as dual stakeholders, pick a target user, and design around their combined needs. Split tracking metrics into online and offline distribution channels to verify intended outcomes.

question: Design an app for tracking delivery partners at a B2B e-commerce company.
hint: Structure your answer by mapping current tasks and user behaviour, defining the delivery-partner persona, listing goals and pain points per journey step, proposing solutions with wireframes, prioritising features, setting success metrics, and outlining a launch plan.

question: What is your favourite product and why? Walk me through your reasoning.
How would you improve the favourite product you just described?
You are a PM at a company that wants to build a new product for Indian households. How would you approach this?
hint: The prompt is deliberately open-ended; use clarifying questions to narrow scope quickly. Expect deep cross-questioning on pricing strategy, GTM approach, household-count estimates, and target customer prioritisation.

question: Design an investment app for users aged 16 to 25.
hint: Design an app that builds a savings habit for this age group by presenting diverse investment options accessibly and guiding users to make their first investment decision.

question: Design a smart refrigerator for urban working professionals.
hint: Use the CIRCLES framework. Map working-professional pain points—food expiry tracking, grocery restocking reminders, meal planning—and design features accordingly. Justify every assumption you make, as interviewers will probe each one.

question: Walmart's PS5 sales on its app dropped sharply after Christmas. What caused the decline?
hint: Investigate logistics and delivery timelines first. Customers purchasing holiday gifts require on-time delivery; repeated delivery-time breaches during the holiday period would erode trust and suppress conversion.

question: How would you improve and monetise Google Maps? Sketch wireframes to illustrate your key proposals.
hint: Map all stakeholder types—cab drivers, logistics operators, food-delivery executives, public transport, ambulances. Prioritise transportation and food-delivery segments on scale and monetisation potential. Proposed solutions included terrain-optimised routing data and real-time delivery-demand prediction.

question: The number of inactive accounts on a streaming platform (like Hotstar) has risen significantly. What is causing this, and how would you investigate it?
hint: Separate internal and external factors. In one scenario the root cause was the platform losing IPL broadcast rights, which triggered mass user migration to a competitor—an external and content-licensing cause rather than a product bug.

question: You are the PM at Hotstar. Having lost the IPL broadcast rights, how would you reduce inactive users and grow viewership without being able to re-acquire IPL?
hint: Apply a standard product-design framework to identify substitute engagement drivers—original content, other marquee sports, regional-language content—that can replace the engagement gap left by the lost IPL contract.

question: Design sunglasses for two-to-three-year-old children.

Name a product you personally use every day, identify one of your own pain points with it, and propose a feature to address that pain point. Then define what metrics you would track as PM for that feature and explain why.
hint: Ground the problem in a genuine personal pain point rather than a hypothetical persona. Articulate the problem clearly, propose the feature, then break metrics into a north-star metric and secondary supporting indicators. Discuss data-collection methods, including qualitative tools like user surveys.

question: COVID disrupted local businesses and widened the gap between consumers and neighbourhood shops. Design an app and a go-to-market strategy to reconnect local retailers with customers.
